body.translated_text:
(Now, the first chapter)
[Section on the four prerequisites]

1.1.1: From the true knowledge of the [sixteen] categories—means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), objects of valid knowledge (<s>prameya</s>), doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), purpose (<s>prayojana</s>), example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>), established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), members of a syllogism (<s>avayava</s>), hypothetical reasoning (<s>tarka</s>), ascertainment (<s>nirṇaya</s>), honest debate (<s>vāda</s>), sophistic debate (<s>jalpa</s>), destructive debate (<s>vitaṇḍā</s>), fallacious reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>), quibbling (<s>chala</s>), futile rejoinders (<s>jāti</s>), and points of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>)—[comes] the attainment of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>).
{Sūtra enumerating the categories}

1.1.2: From the successive elimination of suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), birth (<s>janma</s>), activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), defects (<s>doṣa</s>), and false knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>)—each being eliminated by the elimination of the one following it—[comes] final liberation (<s>apavarga</s>).
{Sūtra enumerating the categories}
Section on means of valid knowledge
1.1.3: The means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) are perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), comparison (<s>upamāna</s>), and verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>).
{Sūtra enumerating the means of valid knowledge}

body.text: 1.1.4: indriyārthasannikarṣotpannam jñānam avyapadeśyam avyabhicāri vyavasāyātmakam pratyakṣam
body.translated_text: 1.1.4: Perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is the knowledge that arises from the contact of a sense organ with its object, which is non-verbal (<s>avyapadeśya</s>), non-errant (<s>avyabhicāri</s>), and of the nature of determinate cognition (<s>vyavasāyātmaka</s>).
{Definition of perception}

body.text: 1.1.5: atha tatpūrvakaṃ trividham anumānaṃ pūrvavat śeṣavat sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ ca
body.translated_text: 1.1.5: Now, inference (<s>anumāna</s>), which is preceded by that [perception], is threefold: <s>pūrvavat</s> (from cause to effect), <s>śeṣavat</s> (from effect to cause), and <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (from general observation).
{Definition of inference}
1.1.6: Comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) is the means of knowing the thing to be established (<s>sādhya</s>) from its similarity with a well-known thing.
{Definition of comparison}
1.1.7: Verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) is the instruction of a reliable person (<s>āpta</s>).
{Definition of verbal testimony}
1.1.8: It is twofold, because [it pertains to] seen and unseen objects.
{Division of verbal testimony}
Section on objects of valid knowledge

1.1.9: The objects of valid knowledge (<s>prameya</s>) are: the self (<s>ātman</s>), the body (<s>śarīra</s>), the sense organs (<s>indriya</s>), the objects of sense (<s>artha</s>), cognition (<s>buddhi</s>), the mind (<s>manas</s>), activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), defects (<s>doṣa</s>), transmigration (<s>pretyabhāva</s>), fruit [of action] (<s>phala</s>), suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>).
{Sūtra enumerating objects of valid knowledge}

1.1.10: Desire (<s>icchā</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), effort (<s>prayatna</s>), pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), and cognition (<s>jñāna</s>) are the marks (<s>liṅga</s>) of the self (<s>ātman</s>).
{Definition of the self}
1.1.11: The body (<s>śarīra</s>) is the locus of effort, sense organs, and objects [of experience].
{Definition of the body}
1.1.12: The sense organs (<s>indriya</s>) are the nose, tongue, eye, skin, and ear, [which arise] from the elements.
{Definition of the sense organs}

body.text: 1.1.13: pṛthivī āpaḥ tejaḥ vāyuḥ ākāśam iti bhūtāni
body.translated_text: 1.1.13: The elements (<s>bhūta</s>) are earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>), water (<s>āpas</s>), fire (<s>tejas</s>), wind (<s>vāyu</s>), and space (<s>ākāśa</s>).
{Definition of the elements}
1.1.14: Smell, taste, color, touch, and sound are the qualities of earth and the rest, [and are] the objects (<s>artha</s>) of those [sense organs].
{Definition of the objects of sense}
1.1.15: <s>Buddhi</s> (cognition), <s>upalabdhi</s> (apprehension), and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) are synonymous.
{Definition of cognition}
1.1.16: The non-simultaneous arising of cognitions is the mark of the mind (<s>manas</s>).
{Definition of mind}
1.1.17: Activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) is the initiation of speech, mind, and body.
{Definition of activity}
1.1.18: Defects (<s>doṣa</s>) are characterized by [their capacity for] instigating [activity].
{Definition of defects}
1.1.19: Transmigration (<s>pretyabhāva</s>) is rebirth.
{Definition of transmigration}
1.1.20: Fruit (<s>phala</s>) is the result produced by activity and defects.
{Definition of fruit}
1.1.21: Suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) is characterized by affliction.
{Definition of suffering}
1.1.22: Liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) is the absolute release from that [suffering].
{Definition of liberation}
Section on the definitions of the preliminary components of reasoning

body.text: 1.1.23: samānānekadharmopapatteḥ vipratipatteḥ upalabdhyanupalabdhyavyavasthātaḥ ca viśeṣāpekṣaḥ vimarśaḥ saṃśayaḥ
body.translated_text: 1.1.23: Doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) is a vacillating cognition with regard to a particular, arising from the apprehension of properties common [to several things], from conflicting testimony, and from the indeterminacy of perception and non-perception.
{Definition of doubt}

body.text: 1.1.24: yam artham adhikṛtya pravartate tat prayojanam
body.translated_text: 1.1.24: Purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) is that with reference to which one proceeds.
{Definition of purpose}

body.text: 1.1.25: laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ yasmin arthe buddhisāmyam saḥ dṛṣṭāntaḥ
body.translated_text: 1.1.25: An example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) is a matter on which ordinary people and investigators have the same understanding.
{Definition of example}
Section on the definition of established conclusions, the basis of reasoning
1.1.26: An established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>) is a position established in a system, in a topic, or by acceptance.
{Definition of accepted established conclusion}

1.1.27: It is fourfold, because of the difference between conclusions of all systems (<s>sarvatantra</s>), of a particular system (<s>pratitantra</s>), of a topic under discussion (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), and by acceptance (<s>abhyupagama</s>).
{Sūtra enumerating the divisions of established conclusions}
1.1.28: A conclusion of all systems (<s>sarvatantrasiddhānta</s>) is a position accepted in a [particular] system that is not contradicted by any system.
{Definition of a conclusion of all systems}
1.1.29: A conclusion of a particular system (<s>pratitantrasiddhānta</s>) is one established in one's own system but not established in an opposing system.
{Definition of a conclusion of a particular system}
1.1.30: A topical conclusion (<s>adhikaraṇasiddhānta</s>) is one whose establishment leads to the establishment of another topic.
{Definition of a topical conclusion}
1.1.31: An accepted conclusion (<s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s>) is the examination of the implications of a position that has been accepted without prior investigation.
{Definition of an accepted conclusion}
Section on the syllogism

1.1.32: The members (<s>avayava</s>) [of a syllogism] are: the proposition (<s>pratijñā</s>), the reason (<s>hetu</s>), the example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>), the application (<s>upanaya</s>), and the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>).
{Sūtra enumerating the members}
1.1.33: The proposition (<s>pratijñā</s>) is the statement of what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>).
{Definition of the proposition}
1.1.34: The reason (<s>hetu</s>) is the means of establishing what is to be proved, through similarity with the example.
{Definition of the reason}
1.1.35: Likewise through dissimilarity.
{Definition of the reason}
1.1.36: An example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>) is an instance that possesses the property of what is to be proved, [presented] through similarity with the <s>sādhya</s>.
{Definition of the example}
1.1.37: Or the reverse of that, through dissimilarity.
{Definition of the example}

body.text: 1.1.38: udāharaṇāpekṣaḥ tathā iti upasaṃhāraḥ na tathā iti vā sādhyasya upanayaḥ
body.translated_text: 1.1.38: The application (<s>upanaya</s>) is the subsumption of the <s>sādhya</s> [under the reason], with reference to the example, [stating] "it is so" or "it is not so."
{Definition of the application}
1.1.39: The conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>) is the restatement of the proposition, after the citation of the reason.
{Definition of the conclusion}
Section on the subsequent components of reasoning

body.text: 1.1.40: avijñātatatve arthe kāraṇopapattitaḥ tattvajñānārtham uhaḥ tarkaḥ
body.translated_text: 1.1.40: Hypothetical reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) is a conjecture for the purpose of knowing the true nature of an object whose nature is not [yet] known, through the propriety of a reason.
{Definition of hypothetical reasoning}
1.1.41: Ascertainment (<s>nirṇaya</s>) is the determination of a matter through deliberation upon the thesis and the counter-thesis.
{Definition of ascertainment}
(Thus ends the first lesson of the first chapter of the <s>Nyāyasūtra</s>)
(Now, the second lesson)
Section on the definition of types of debate

1.2.1: Honest debate (<s>vāda</s>) is the adoption of a thesis and counter-thesis, supported by means of valid knowledge, hypothetical reasoning, and proof and censure, not contrary to any established conclusion, and furnished with the five members [of a syllogism].
{Definition of honest debate}

1.2.2: Sophistic debate (<s>jalpa</s>) is [a debate] furnished as described above, [but also employing] proof and censure through quibbling (<s>chala</s>), futile rejoinders (<s>jāti</s>), and points of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>).
{Definition of sophistic debate}
1.2.3: That [debate] which is devoid of the establishment of a counter-thesis is destructive debate (<s>vitaṇḍā</s>).
{Definition of destructive debate}
Section on fallacious reasons

1.2.4: Fallacious reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) are: the erratic (<s>savyabhicāra</s>), the contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), the one equivalent to the topic (<s>prakaraṇasama</s>), the one equivalent to the thing to be proved (<s>sādhyasama</s>), and the one that is untimely (<s>kālātīta</s>).
{Sūtra enumerating fallacious reasons}
1.2.5: The erratic (<s>savyabhicāra</s>) is the inconclusive [reason].
{Definition of the erratic reason}
1.2.6: The contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) is [a reason] that, having accepted an established conclusion, contradicts it.
{Definition of the contradictory reason}
1.2.7: That which is adduced for the purpose of ascertainment because of which the very topic is under investigation is the one equivalent to the topic (<s>prakaraṇasama</s>).
{Definition of the reason equivalent to the topic}
1.2.8: The one equivalent to the thing to be proved (<s>sādhyasama</s>) is [a reason] not distinct from the <s>sādhya</s>, because of itself requiring proof.
{Definition of the reason equivalent to the sādhya}
1.2.9: The untimely (<s>kālātīta</s>) is [a reason] adduced past the [proper] time.
{Definition of the untimely reason}
Section on quibbling
1.2.10: Quibbling (<s>chala</s>) is the opposition to a statement through the supposition of an alternative meaning.
{Definition of quibbling}

body.text: 1.2.11: tat trividham - vākchalam sāmānyacchalam upacāracchalam ca iti
body.translated_text: 1.2.11: It is threefold: verbal quibbling (<s>vākchala</s>), quibbling on generality (<s>sāmānyacchala</s>), and quibbling on figurative expression (<s>upacāracchala</s>).
{Sūtra enumerating the divisions of quibbling}

body.text: 1.2.12: aviśeṣābhihite arthe vaktuḥ abhiprāyāt arthāntarakalpanā vākchalam
body.translated_text: 1.2.12: Verbal quibbling (<s>vākchala</s>) is the supposition of an alternative meaning, different from the speaker's intention, when the word used is non-specific.
{Definition of verbal quibbling}
1.2.13: Quibbling on generality (<s>sāmānyacchala</s>) is the supposition of a non-existent meaning through an over-generalized application, when the actual meaning is possible.
{Definition of quibbling on generality}
1.2.14: Quibbling on figurative expression (<s>upacāracchala</s>) is the denial of the actual existence of a thing when it is described with a distinction of attributes.
{Definition of quibbling on figurative expression}
1.2.15: [Objection:] Quibbling on figurative expression is just verbal quibbling, because there is no [real] difference between them.
{Objection regarding quibbling on figurative expression}
1.2.16: [Reply:] No, because it is a different matter.
{Definition of quibbling on figurative expression}
1.2.17: Or, if there is no difference, then from some partial similarity, there would be the absurd consequence of all [types] being one [type of] quibbling.
{Definition of quibbling on figurative expression}
Section on the general [features of
defective marks]
1.2.18: A futile rejoinder (<s>jāti</s>) is a counter-argument based on [mere] similarity or dissimilarity.
{Definition of futile rejoinder}
1.2.19: A point of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>) is misunderstanding (<s>vipratipatti</s>) or non-understanding (<s>apratipatti</s>).
{Definition of point of defeat}
1.2.20: The multiplicity of futile rejoinders and points of defeat is due to [their] varieties.
{Sūtra on the multiplicity of points of defeat}
(Thus ends the second lesson of the first chapter of the <s>Nyāyasūtra</s>)
(The first chapter is complete)
(Now, the second chapter)
Section on the examination of objects (<s>viṣaya</s>)
Section on the examination of inference (<s>anumāna</s>)
Section on the examination of analogy (<s>upamāna</s>)
(Thus ends the first lesson of the second book of the <s>Nyāyasūtra</s>.)

(Second lesson)
[Section on the examination of the fourfold classification of <s>pramāṇas</s>]
Section on the examination of the impermanence of sound (sūtras 13-39)
Section on the examination of the transformation of sound (sūtras 40-56)
Section on the examination of the denotative power of words

2.2.60: Those [words], ending in case-suffixes, are <s>pada</s> (a word). {sūtra defining a word}
2.2.61: Doubt [arises] because of figurative usage in the proximity of individual (<s>vyakti</s>), configuration (<s>ākṛti</s>), and genus (<s>jāti</s>). {objection sūtra}
Sub-section on the theory of the individual (vyakti)
Sub-section on the theory of configuration (ākṛti)
2.2.65: [A word denotes] configuration (<s>ākṛti</s>), because the establishment of the designation of beings depends on it. {objection sūtra}
Sub-section on the theory of genus (jāti)

2.2.66: Even when individual and configuration are [both] present, because of the inapplicability of sprinkling and the like to [merely] a lump of clay in the shape of a cow — [a word denotes] the genus (<s>jāti</s>). {objection sūtra}
2.2.67: No, because the manifestation of genus depends on configuration and individual. {established conclusion sūtra}
Sub-section on the established view
(Thus ends the second section of the second chapter of the <s>Nyāyasūtra</s>.)
And this second chapter is concluded.
Incidental section: Examination of the non-duality of the eye (7-14)
Section: Examination of the distinction between <s>ātman</s> (self) and <s>manas</s> (mind) (15-17)
Section: Examination of the body (27-31)
Section: Examination of the sense organs (32-51)
Section: Examination of the plurality of senses (52-62)
Section: Examination of the objects of the senses (62-73)
(Thus ends the first lesson of the third chapter of the <s>Nyāyasūtra</s>)
(The second lesson)
Section: Examination of the impermanence of cognition (1-9)
Section: Examination of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) (10-17)
Section on the examination of whether cognition is a quality of the self (18-41)
Section on the examination of whether cognition is produced and ceases (42-45)
Section on the examination of the distinction of cognition from the qualities of the body (46-55)
Section on the examination of the mind (56-59)
Section on the examination of production through unseen merit (60-72)
(Thus ends the second lesson of the third chapter of the <s>Nyāyasūtra</s>)
(The third chapter is complete)

[Section on the general examination of activity and faults (1-2)]

Refutation of universal permanence (29-33)

Section on the examination of the fruit [of action
Section on the examination of suffering (55-58)
Section on the examination of liberation (59-68)
(Thus the first lesson of the fourth chapter of the <s>Nyāyasūtra</s>.)
Incidental section on the composite whole (4-17)
Preparatory section on partless [entities
Section on the refutation of the denial of external objects (26-37)
Section on the Growth of Knowledge of Reality (sūtras 38-49)
Section on the Preservation of Knowledge of Reality (sūtras 50-51)
(Thus ends the second lesson of the fourth chapter of the <s>Nyāyasūtra</s>.)
(And the fourth chapter is concluded.)
Section on the Two Pseudo-Refutations of Achievability-Equal and Non-Achievability-Equal (sūtras 7-8)

(Thus ends the first lesson of the fifth chapter of the <s>Nyāyasūtra</s>.)
(Second lesson.)

body.text:
5.2.1: pratijñāhāniḥ pratijñāntaraṃ pratijñāvirodhaḥ pratijñāsannyāso hetvantaram arthāntaraṃ nirarthakam avijñātārtham apārthakam aprāpta kālaṃ nyūnam adhikaṃ punaruktam ananubhāṣaṇam ajñānam apratibhā vikṣepo matānujñā paryanuyojyopekṣaṇaṃ niranuyojyānuyogo 'pasiddhānto hetvā bhāsāśca nigrahasthānāni
{nigrahasthāna-uddeśa-sūtram}
body.translated_text:
5.2.1: Abandoning the thesis (<s>pratijñāhāni</s>), shifting to another thesis (<s>pratijñāntara</s>), contradicting the thesis (<s>pratijñāvirodha</s>), renouncing the thesis (<s>pratijñāsannyāsa</s>), shifting to another reason (<s>hetvantara</s>), shifting to another topic (<s>arthāntara</s>), meaninglessness (<s>nirarthaka</s>), unintelligibility (<s>avijñātārtha</s>), incoherence (<s>apārthaka</s>), untimeliness (<s>aprāptakāla</s>), deficiency (<s>nyūna</s>), excess (<s>adhika</s>), repetition (<s>punarukta</s>), failure to respond (<s>ananubhāṣaṇa</s>), ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>), inability to reply (<s>apratibhā</s>), evasion (<s>vikṣepa</s>), conceding the opponent's position (<s>matānujñā</s>), overlooking what is censurable (<s>paryanuyojyopekṣaṇa</s>), censuring what is not censurable (<s>niranuyojyānuyoga</s>), deviation from the established doctrine (<s>apasiddhānta</s>), and pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) — these are the points of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>).
{Enumeration of the points of defeat}
Section on five points of defeat (2-6)
Section on four points of defeat (7-10)
Section on three points of defeat (11-13)
Section on points of defeat concerning repetition (14-16)
Section on four points of defeat concerning failure to respond (17-20)
Section on three points of defeat concerning admission (21-23)
Section on two points of defeat stated by the debaters themselves (24-25)

body.text:
(iti nyāyasūtre pañcamādhyāyasya dvitīyam āhnikam)
(samāptaścāyam pañcamādhyāyaḥ)
nyāyadarśanaṃ samāptam
body.translated_text:
(Thus ends the second lesson of the fifth book of the <s>Nyāyasūtra</s>.)
(The fifth book is complete.)
The <s>Nyāyadarśana</s> (System of Logic) is concluded.
